spans.text: Several months later, in an abandoned underground clinic in the Yellow Zone.
The sound of a newborn's cry echoes through the hallways, bringing the hope of new life to a clinic that has long been filled with wails of misery and suffering.
On the sickbed, a woman in black opens her eyes as her strength returns. She sits up on the bed.
Madam, God has blessed you with a healthy baby boy.
The doctor is all smiles and carefully delivers the baby into his mother's arms.
Surprisingly enough, the woman in black does not rejoice or cry as expected. Instead she simply glances at the baby with cold eyes, and her brow furrows in frustration.
The child bears quite a strong resemblance to Gleb. Even the birthmark on his chest is the same.
...Send him to 13th Street.
Don't you... wish to look at your son?
This is not a blessing from God, but a curse...
Do as I say, or he will bring great misfortune upon you.
The baby in her arms seems to sense his mother's indifference and cries loudly.
However, the woman in black does not spare him an ounce of pity and slowly struggles to rise from the bed. She trudges out of the clinic, one step at a time...
Sakharov's choice is a good one.
Just a few months after Valeriya joined the Vory, she has settled several gang feuds with unprecedented force and removed many obstacles for the Vory.
However, Valeriya has been taking more and more leaves of absence within the past month, and Sakharov started to grow suspicious.
She knows that she must not waste too much time on a trivial matter... She has to regain Sakharov's trust at today's meeting.
Good afternoon, my dear Valyusha.
Valeriya enters the room and sees Sakharov turning from the window, his face all smiles.
He is holding a newborn baby in his arms.
Valeriya's eyes go wide; the birthmark on the baby is—
I see...
Valeriya nods and walks up to Sakharov. She glances coldly at the baby that is sound asleep.
He looks very cute, doesn't he?
This is a life that should never have existed. Please permit me to eliminate it without delay.
Sakharov sizes up Valeriya, but he does not see a single ripple in her eyes.
He sighs inwardly, and then orders someone to have the baby taken out.
Have a seat, dear Valyusha.
Sakharov's face is gentle and kind, but also commanding. Valeriya has no choice but to sit down with him, staring deeply into those unreadable, gleaming eyes.
You see, this is what happened—last night, Satan came into my dream and gave me a great prophecy.
He told me that today, I would receive an adopted child with blood ties to the next leader of the Vory. Otherwise, ill fortune would befall me...
I do not understand.
Valyusha, do you not think that all this is fate?
In my heart, you are the one in whom I have the most faith. And Satan has given me a dream, while you have been given a son today...
Clearly, it is a sign that this child should not be killed, but that I should adopt him as a son.
But the Vory must forsake all family.
Relax. Everyone who knows about this has been eliminated.
Right now, only you and I know the true identity of this child.
Valeriya frowns slightly and considers Sakharov's words. Going against him now would not be wise.
Plus, the Vory are all devout Satan worshippers, and they will not allow Valeriya to deny this "prophecy".
I do not care if the child lives or dies.
But if Satan wills it, and if you insist, then... I shall abide by your decision.
Very good, very good...
Sakharov smiles warmly and gently squeezes Valeriya's hand.
I've decided. His name will be Nikolai.
From now onward, I will declare Nikolai my adopted son. He will grow up happily by my side—and it will be none of your concern.
In the Devil's name, Nikolai will bear witness to the agreement between us.
Valeriya nods in gratitude and kisses Sakharov's hand.
Then, she leaves the room as the "Chief Financier" favors her with a warm, caring look.
What a ruthless woman she is.
Gloominess suddenly creeps across Sakharov's face.
A Vor enters the room holding the baby and bows politely to Sakharov.
Why did you not kill that woman if you were wary of her? We could have...
Her status now makes her untouchable.
Besides, our organization needs her. Only someone as ruthless as her can lead the Vory to rule over the Yellow Zone...
Unfortunately, I am old, and if she decides to do something out of line... I need some kind of leverage to feel at ease.
Pakhan, you don't have to worry. We'll do our best to protect you no matter what she's scheming!
What can you do...
Sakharov smiles gently, but he doesn't bother hiding the mockery in his words. The Vor bows his head as he realizes his impotence.
I think I understand what Gleb was trying to do, and it even makes sense...
People without weaknesses are the most frightening, and given how perfect and powerful Valeriya is, we have no choice but to create a weakness in her.
Isn't that right, little Nikolai?
Nikolai giggles in Sakharov's arms, an innocent, pure, and endearing angel.
